passages: California has developed AskCA, a new AI-powered tool to help Californians better connect with state services through a streamlined model designed around life events like finding a job, starting a business, or recovering from a disaster. The state is now seeking volunteers to help test and refine this new tool.
Starting today, Californians can sign up to be part of the pilot.
Testers must be 18 years or older and a California resident.
The prototype was built by the Office of Data and Innovation to navigate people through life events including, for example:
The California Office of Data and Innovation built AskCA’s knowledge base in collaboration with Anthropic’s Claude model, with security support from the California Department of Technology.
CalHR is the first department to deploy the AskCA prototype in a live public service, powering a new AI‑driven job‑skills‑matching feature launching September 30 on CalCareers.ca.gov.
Subject matter experts from across state government are continually helping to inform the responses to improve AskCA’s accuracy.

Be 18 years or older
Live in California

passages: This is a prototype. By signing up for the pilot testing, your feedback will help us improve it. It may not always get things right — every question you ask helps us make it better.

We're making it easier. Tell us what you're going through — whether that's finding a state job, recovering from a disaster, or having a child — and we'll help you find the right programs, services, and next steps.
No government jargon. No personal information. Just tell us what you're dealing with.
We pull from state, federal, and county sources in real time to find accurate answers.
We give you clear next steps and direct links. You spend less time searching.
We do NOT train the model based on your conversations.
Our team reviews conversations to find gaps and catch errors.

passages: September 9, 2026

AskCA is a prototype developed by the state’s Office of Data and Innovation to help Californians find resources based on life events, such as finding a job, starting a business, accessing family services and recovering from disasters.

California’s next test will be whether AskCA can move beyond retrieval toward actually connecting residents with government services. The state is seeking Californians to beta test the tool, while CalHR plans to deploy its technology for AI-powered job matching starting Sept. 30.
records.limitation: Independent reporting of the announcement and open effectiveness question; it supplies no measured AskCA accuracy or public-service outcome.
